_comment: Per-model bench sampling overrides. Read by scripts/bench/bench_runner.py.
The scored inspect_ai tasks (gsm8k, humaneval, humaneval_plus, mmlu_pro,
gpqa, tools) run at temperature=0 by default -- greedy decoding is what
docs/sampling-strategies.md prescribes for deterministic eval, and it is
what the two sidecar tasks (bench_longctx, bench_latency_leak) have always
pinned. Before that default existed the tasks passed NO sampling
parameters at all, so each backend applied its own, and vLLM / SGLang /
Ollama do not default the same -- two models benched on different engines
were not being compared under the same conditions.
A few models cannot be benched greedily. This file is the escape hatch,
keyed by catalog model name, matched as a substring of the serving alias.
Recording an override here makes that model's rows NOT directly comparable
with the greedy ones. That is the lesser evil: the alternative is a score
of ~0 that looks like a capability result but is really a sampling
artifact. Say why in `reason` so the next reader does not 'fix' it back.
Any omitted field falls back to the BENCH_TEMPERATURE / BENCH_TOP_P

NVIDIA-Nemotron-Nano-9B-v2-NVFP4.reason: Loops on greedy reasoning: at temperature 0 the <think> trace runs away and no answer is ever emitted, so every scored task reads ~0 and looks like a capability failure. 0.6 / 0.95 is NVIDIA's recommended Nemotron sampling. Documented against the family in scripts/model-families.yaml (nemotron-nano-v2).
